text: So the Digital Dollar Project is a nonprofit, nonpartisan, non governmentally funded, we're self funded think tank and it's focused really on. So I founded it when I left the commission in 2019. And we have a broad based advisory board, we publish papers, we do conferences. We're focused on three very simple but very important questions. One, how do we future proof the dollar for the coming digital world, or I should say is world of digital networks of value? How do we preserve the dollar's reserve currency status? And really, maybe most importantly, how do we preserve the dollar's embodiment of the values that have made the dollar the world's most aspirational currency? Values of free enterprise, values of free, free economic autonomy and values of the appropriate balance between law enforcement and economic liberty. And how do we do all those things in a world that is increasingly becoming one where value will move along rails, some of which are centralized by governments, some of which are centralized by corporates, some of which are highly decentralized. How do we do all those things in a dollar context? And that's the work of the Digital Dollar Project.

So the future is going to be all of the above. And what we need to make sure is anything that references the dollar adheres to the principles on which the dollar is based. So in a recent working paper published by the Digital Dollar Project in February, we looked at all forms of digital networks of money from these principles of future proofing the dollar, preserving its reserve currency status and, and most importantly, preserving the values. Now to your question, what's the difference? Well, in the future we are going to have a digital tokenized accounts which will be dollar based. We are going to have stablecoins which will be dollar based. Some of those will be run by broad banks, some of those stablecoins, some of them will be run by narrow banks.
